_comment: What a remote request is allowed to become on a machine that has offered
itself to Huginn. THE SINGLE SOURCE — three programs need to agree about
this and they are written in three languages:
The first two BUILD THE ARGV — they are the enforcement. The third only
decides whether to bother offering the work, so a person is told 'that
machine is locked' at the moment they ask rather than a minute later.
Kept declarative because the failure mode of drift is not a wrong pixel: a
runner that granted Bash where this file says look would be a silent hole in
the fence around somebody's personal computer, and nothing would look wrong.
scripts/gen-device-policy.js expands this into the Kotlin table, the headless
runner's embedded copy, and the case matrix both implementations are tested
against. server/appd/test/device-policy-cases.test.js fails if any of them has
drifted from this file — which is why deploy.sh cannot ship a drifted daemon.

look._comment: Note what is not here: no Bash. And it is DENIED as well as un-granted, because Claude Code's safe-Bash classification is content-dependent — two near-identical commands a minute apart were approved and then refused. From the far end that reads as a fence that works and then does not. Deny is deterministic.

refusals.locked: this machine is locked, so it is read-only until someone unlocks it
refusals.scope: this machine is set to {scope}, which cannot run {mode}
